executive_summary: AUD/CHF closed at 0.57643 on 2026-10-02 (Swiss francs per Australian dollar; a rising pair means a stronger AUD). It is down 0.88% over one month, up 2.89% over three months, up 2.94% over six months and up 11.14% over one year, and it sits at the 86th percentile of its 52-week closing range. The pair rests on the widest policy gap in the G10: the RBA is at 4.60% after its unanimous hike on 29 September, and the SNB is at 0.00% after a fifth straight hold. The settled pass-1 verdict is Bullish tactically at conviction 3 (score +0.3541) and Bullish strategically at conviction 2 (score +0.1386). What makes this cross unusual is that the two currency dossiers reinforce each other. The AUD dossier is tactically Bullish AUD and the CHF dossier is tactically Bearish CHF, and on this cross both point the same way. That case is offset by three bilateral facts: (1) Crowded franc short: leveraged funds are short CHF at -12.3% of open interest, with open interest down 22.1% in a single week. (2) External accounts: Australia runs a current account deficit of 3.67% of GDP against Switzerland's 9.20% surplus, a 12.9-point gap. (3) Valuation: Australia's real effective exchange rate is 116.11 against Switzerland's 99.87, a 16-point gap. The carry is concrete. It is worth about 21.8 pips a month and about 133 pips over six months. The six-month breakeven, 0.56313, lands almost exactly on the base of the six-touch 0.56309–0.5672 support band. I flag one disagreement without re-scoring. The 91-pip drop on 1 October, the widest daily range in the 130-session window, came the same day Switzerland's September CPI printed 1.0%. The CHF dossier records that print as post-cut context. It weakens the premise in Factors 1 and 6 that the market's December SNB hike pricing is overdone. I would hold the direction but put less weight on the guidance leg than pass 1 did. The plan is to: buy on dips into the 0.5706–0.5743 band; exit on a daily close below 0.5665; target 0.5812–0.5853 tactically; and treat the strategic position as a carry hold rather than a call for the price to rise, given the pair's tendency to fall sharply in risk-off episodes.

market_context.valuation_assessment: The two dossiers' valuation methods disagree in sign, and that disagreement is itself the main finding. World Bank PPP (AUD dossier) implies AUD/CHF 0.66532, i.e. AUD ~12% cheap and the pair 'should' be higher; the REER-relative proxy (CHF dossier) implies 0.50105, i.e. AUD ~14% rich and the pair 'should' be lower. The REER method is the more relevant one for a six-month view. Australia's real effective exchange rate is 116.11, the highest in the G10+SGD set and up 9.97% in a year. Switzerland's is 99.87, down 2.83% and almost exactly at its base-period level. In real terms the base currency has had the largest one-year appreciation in the block while its main export price, iron ore, fell 7.14%. The quote currency has cheapened while its external surplus widened. The PPP figure is a price-level measure and has no predictive power over six months. What the current level reflects is carry and nothing else. The real gap is the reason Factor 5's strategic stance is Bearish. Neither valuation signal is actionable within four weeks. Outside cross-check: the ATO year-end series puts the nearest actual exchange rate at 30 June 2026 at 0.5564, matching the payload's late-June closes in the 0.556–0.559 area.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The policy-rate carry is +460bp (RBA 4.60% less SNB 0.00%), the widest bilateral spread in the G10+SGD matrix. The listed futures roll from 6A/6S (December 2026 to March 2027, observed 2026-09-30) pays -488.6bp annualised, 28.6bp wider than the policy spread; the difference combines cross-currency basis and term effects and cannot be split without an OIS curve. It is a funding premium, not a policy differential. Carry-to-vol is 0.73 on estimated 3M IV of 6.282% (conservative figure carried from the verdict), 0.78 on 60-day realised 5.92% and 0.88 on 20-day realised 5.24%; on any of these it is the best risk-adjusted carry in the AUD complex (AUD/USD's equivalent is 0.117). Carry regime is working: VIX is 16.07, US investment-grade spreads 83bp and equities within about 2% of record highs; the pair rose 11.14% over the year while also paying the differential. The three breakeven cushions line up almost exactly with the three structural supports. Forward points are derived by linear extrapolation from the -488.6bp futures roll; on a pure 460bp policy basis the points would be -22.1, -66.3 and -132.6 pips.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is 460bp — RBA Cash Rate Target 4.60% after the unanimous 25bp hike on 29 September against an SNB policy rate of 0.00% held for a fifth consecutive assessment on 24 September. That is the widest policy spread available in the G10+SGD set and it widened by 25bp within the last fortnight of September, entirely from the Australian side. The trajectory inside the tactical window can only widen or hold: the RBA decides on 2026-11-03 with a retained explicit option to raise further, while the SNB does not decide until 2026-12-10, outside the tactical window, so there is no scheduled Swiss event through which the gap can narrow. On pricing, the asymmetry is unusually clean in the pair's favour: roughly 20% of a 25bp RBA hike is discounted for 3 November, while the Swiss curve carries nearly 50% of a December SNB hike and around 75bp by September 2027 — the market is underpricing the hawkish leg and overpricing the dovish leg of the same cross simultaneously. Transmission is direct and mechanical: a long AUD/CHF position accrues roughly 21.8 pips of carry a month at 460bp on a 0.57643 spot, and the executable futures roll is wider still at -488.6bp annualised, 28.6bp beyond the policy spread, the wedge being cross-currency basis plus term effects that cannot be separated without an OIS curve. The 10-year leg corroborates rather than contradicts: Australia yields roughly 481bp over Switzerland on the dossiers' live cross-section, wider than the policy gap itself.

Both halves of that have to be right for the differential to narrow, and only one scheduled meeting inside the window can move either.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the question is the direction of the 460bp gap rather than its level, and the honest answer is that it holds near its maximum rather than widening much further. On the Australian side the RBA is at or near terminal: one more 25bp step by February 2027 is plausible at the 2026-11-03 or 2026-12-08 decisions, but unemployment at a post-COVID 4.6% and NAB business conditions negative for the first time since September 2020 cap how far the cycle can run. On the Swiss side the SNB sits at a 0.00% floor with core inflation at 0.40% and nominal wage growth at 0.40%, so it cannot ease without going negative — a question neither the June nor the September 2026 documents even discuss — and its own conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% is constructed on an unchanged rate through 2028. The strategic edge therefore is not in widening but in the resolution of the market's Swiss hike pricing at the single scheduled decision inside the horizon, 2026-12-10: if the SNB confirms its own forecast, roughly 75bp of embedded tightening leaves the Swiss front end and the differential is re-rated wider in forward space without either central bank moving. Transmission remains carry: 460bp over six months is approximately 133 pips of accrual against a 0.57643 spot, a cushion no other G10 cross offers, and the carry-to-vol ratio of 0.73 on estimated 3M implied vol is the best risk-adjusted carry in the AUD complex. The constraint is that this is the maximum of the differential, not its midpoint, so the factor is an income stream with a known ceiling rather than a widening trade.

Tactically the differential cannot narrow on any scheduled event — the SNB simply does not meet before 2026-12-10 — so the only live repricing is the Australian one and it is underpriced. tactical.bilateral_analysis: The inflation differential is the widest in the G10 matrix and it points one way. Australian headline monthly CPI re-accelerated to 4.0% year-on-year in August from 3.5%, with trimmed mean stuck at 3.6% for a third month; Swiss headline is 0.80% and core 0.40%, the lowest core reading in the block. That is a 320bp headline gap and a 320bp core gap, and the composition explains why it persists: energy is roughly 3.5% of the Swiss basket against a far larger weight in the Australian one, so the same Brent shock that pushed Australian headline to 4.0% lifted Swiss headline by 40bp. The trajectory inside the tactical window is set by one release, the Australian September quarter CPI on 28 October, which lands five days before the 2026-11-03 RBA decision; a trimmed mean at or above 3.7% reprices that meeting from roughly 20% through 50% and the pair with it. Swiss monthly CPI prints in the first business days of each month and, on the SNB's own 0.7% full-year path, is more likely to undercut Swiss hike pricing than to validate it. The growth differential runs the other way and is the reason confidence is 55 rather than 70: Swiss Q2 GDP grew 1.885% quarter-on-quarter, the fastest in the block, against Australia's 0.42%, with KOF at a five-year high of 109.1 against negative NAB business conditions. The transmission that matters for a 460bp carry pair is the policy channel, not the growth level, and on the policy channel the inflation gap dominates.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the two dossiers turn bearish on their own currencies for different reasons and the effects substantially cancel, which is what a Neutral stance here is recording. On the Australian side the energy shock has stopped being an inflation story and started being a margin story: NAB purchase costs rose 1.2% in the quarter against final product prices of 0.5%, sales margins fell to -20, unemployment reached 4.6% with the entire August employment gain part-time, and real wages fell for a third consecutive quarter. That is the configuration in which a cost-push shock becomes a demand contraction and the market begins pricing an RBA pivot well before the RBA delivers one — pair-negative through the rate channel. On the Swiss side the 200bp core-inflation gap to the ECB and the Fed fixes the SNB last in the global queue regardless of how fast Swiss output grows, SECO's own panel forecasts 0.6% average inflation for both 2026 and 2027, and roughly half of the Q2 Swiss growth beat came from the volatile chemical-pharmaceutical sector with ZEW expectations collapsing from 12.1 to 2.6 — pair-positive through the same channel. Transmission for the pair is the relative distance each central bank sits from its own reaction threshold, and over six months both move toward dovishness at roughly comparable speed from opposite ends. Neither economy's data releases dominate the other's for this cross; the Australian ones are louder but the Swiss ones are the ones that would reprice a 75bp mispricing.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the highest-beta risk pair in the G10 and the risk tape is currently benign in the dimensions that matter for it. VIX closed at 16.07, the 28th percentile of its one-year range; the S&P 500 is up 14.0% over twelve months and within 2% of its record; US investment-grade spreads are 83bp. AUD carries the highest risk beta in the G10 and CHF's return depends on capital flight, so a tape with no flight is a tape in which the pair's two legs push the same way — the Australian dollar earns its beta and the franc earns nothing. The corroboration is unusually clean: gold fell 6.00% over the month, and because gold is the franc's commodity link through shared safe-haven demand rather than trade, that is the same signal measured independently of the equity market. The asymmetry in the tactical window is credit rather than equity: US high-yield widened 42bp over the month to 302bp, the 83rd percentile of its one-year range, and investment grade sits at the 86th percentile of the year even while tight in level — the first evidence that the energy shock is reaching corporate balance sheets. For a pair whose carry cushion is 21.8 pips a month against a currency that can move 2% in an afternoon on a risk event, the credit signal is the one to respect. The transmission is immediate and non-linear: the pair rises slowly on carry and falls quickly on volatility.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk distribution for this pair is wide and its shape is adverse even if its centre is not. The modal path is a continuation of the benign tape — credit tight, equities higher, the Fed tightening into 4.1% unemployment rather than easing into a recession — and on that path the pair grinds higher on carry. But AUD/CHF is the single most convex G10 expression of a volatility event: the base currency has the highest equity beta and the quote currency has the fattest documented tail, with the January 2015 EUR/CHF floor removal moving roughly 30% intraday as the reference case. Two named binaries sit inside the horizon. A Hormuz escalation is a simultaneous oil, equity and credit shock in which Australia is the G10 economy least able to absorb the risk-off and the franc is the first refuge — the clean pair-negative. A French sovereign accident, with OAT-Bund at a one-year high of 111.2bp against a 74.2bp average and a EUR 54bn budget vote pending, routes European capital into francs rather than euros — also pair-negative, and with no offsetting Australian channel at all. Against those, a Hormuz settlement is ambiguous rather than cleanly positive: it lifts global growth and Chinese demand, which is pair-positive, but removes the RBA's stated justification for further tightening, which is pair-negative. The expectation-weighted stance is therefore Neutral with a negatively skewed shape, and the honest statement is that the modal path favours the pair while the tail does not.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Adjusted from default 0.16 strategic: +0.02 strategic. The external-balance gap between these two economies is the widest non-petroleum pairing in the block — a 3.67%-of-GDP deficit against a 9.20%-of-GDP surplus, 12.9 points — and it is the defining structural tension of the cross. tactical.bilateral_analysis: Over four weeks the external differential is large but inert, and the commodity netting is genuinely offsetting. Australia's terms of trade are pulling in opposite directions within themselves: iron ore, roughly 35% of export revenue, sits at USD 96.59 a tonne, up 0.56% on the month but down 7.14% over twelve, while Newcastle coal at USD 145.20 is up 36.72% over the year and copper up 35.84%, with the RBA commodity price index up 15.5% year-on-year. Switzerland has no commodity export exposure at all; its commodity link runs through gold as a shared safe-haven asset, and gold fell 6.00% over the month, which is quote-negative and therefore pair-positive. Set against that, Switzerland is a net energy importer, so Brent near USD 100 is a mild terms-of-trade drag on the quote currency, partly offset by Swiss producer and import prices running at -0.70% year-on-year. Bilateral trade itself is small and dominated by composition rather than cycle: Australia runs a USD 1.6bn goods deficit with Switzerland on 2024 IMF DOTS figures, importing USD 3.0bn against exports of USD 1.4bn, a flow driven largely by Swiss pharmaceutical and precious-metal exports rather than by anything cyclical. None of this generates an identifiable four-week flow, which is why the stance is Neutral; the identifiable tactical sensitivity is to an iron ore break below USD 90 or a gold reversal above the month's highs.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: This is the clearest strategic argument against the pair and it carries the second-heaviest strategic weight. The external differential is 12.9 percentage points of GDP: Australia's current account deficit widened by AUD 1.8bn to AUD 27.2bn, or 3.67% of GDP, with the goods and services balance itself in deficit at AUD 5.1bn and net foreign debt at AUD 1,486bn, while Switzerland runs a 9.20%-of-GDP surplus with a Q2 current account surplus of CHF 24bn, up CHF 13bn year-on-year, a trade surplus that nearly doubled to CHF 23.7bn and a net international investment position of CHF 986bn. One of these economies has a structural financing requirement and the other has a structural capital outflow to recycle. Valuation says the same thing from the other direction and is the more actionable half: the BIS real effective exchange rate puts Australia at 116.11, the highest in the block and up 9.97% over twelve months — the largest real appreciation in the set — against Switzerland at 99.87, down 2.83% and almost exactly at its base period. In other words the base currency has appreciated 9.97% in real terms while its principal export price fell 7.14%, and the quote currency has cheapened while its surplus widened. That is not a configuration that persists for six months, and the variable that historically gives is the exchange rate. The transmission is cumulative rather than event-driven, which is why the factor is weighted at 0.18 strategically and 0.06 tactically.

factors.horizon_split: Neutral tactically and Bearish strategically, following both the weights and the mechanism. Over four weeks a 12.9-point current-account gap produces no identifiable transaction demand and the commodity netting cancels. Over six months cumulative balance-of-payments flows, not sentiment, set real exchange rates, and a base currency 9.97% richer in real terms with a widening deficit against a quote currency 2.83% cheaper with a widening surplus is a financing asymmetry that has to be met at a price. It reinforces the factor's conclusion that this bilateral trade is a composition effect, not a cyclical flow signal.

Mildly positive to oil as a net energy exporter in value terms. RBA commodity price index +15.5% YoY.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: CHF: no direct commodity export exposure. The framework's link is gold, which transmits through shared safe-haven demand rather than trade — gold up is CHF-positive. Switzerland is a net energy importer, so higher oil and gas are a modest terms-of-trade drag, muted by energy being only about 3.5% of the Swiss basket. Precious metals are 39.9% of Swiss goods exports by value, but as a trading and refining flow rather than a terms-of-trade exposure.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Apply the framework's direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: AUD gets a mild positive (+) as a net energy exporter through LNG and coal; CHF gets a mild negative (-) as a net energy importer, amplified for this cross by the fact that the same oil move lifts Australian CPI toward 4.0% while lifting Swiss headline by only 40bp, so the policy-divergence channel compounds the direct terms-of-trade channel. Net: pair rises, and the rate-channel amplification makes the move larger than a pure terms-of-trade netting would suggest. Iron ore up: AUD strongly positive (++), CHF neutral — no offset exists, so iron ore passes through to the pair almost one-for-one. Gold up: AUD neutral to mildly positive as a producer, CHF positive (+) through the safe-haven channel which historically dominates — net pair falls modestly. The dominant netting insight for this cross is that the quote currency has almost no commodity exposure, so Australian terms of trade pass through largely unoffset, while the one commodity that moves the franc, gold, moves it through the risk channel already counted in Factor 3.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Pair rises an estimated 0.4-0.8%. Direct terms of trade contribute little — Australia's energy export gain is real but modest and Switzerland's import cost is small at a 3.5% basket weight. The larger effect is indirect: a further Brent rise keeps Australian headline CPI above 4.0% and sustains the RBA's 'permanently higher' framing into the 2026-11-03 decision while barely touching Swiss core at 0.40%, widening the policy divergence the pair is built on. In pips at 0.57643: +23 to +46 pips, which reaches into the lower edge of the 0.58123 resistance band at the top of the range.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Pair falls an estimated 0.6-1.2% — a larger move than the symmetric rise, because the downside works through two channels at once. Lower Brent removes the supply-side inflation impulse underpinning the RBA's hiking option, which is the pair's primary support, and simultaneously removes the energy-driven Swiss headline rise that has been sustaining the market's ~50% December SNB hike pricing; the second effect is pair-positive but much smaller, since Swiss core at 0.40% was never driven by energy. Net asymmetry is against the pair. In pips at 0.57643: -35 to -69 pips, a range that spans the 0.57056–0.57431 support band and ends just above the 200-week/100-day confluence.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Brent, not iron ore. Iron ore is the larger driver of the Australian terms of trade in isolation, but for THIS cross Brent dominates because it is the variable that sets the relative inflation and therefore the relative policy path of the two central banks — the 460bp differential the pair exists to harvest. Gold is the second-order driver and it works through the franc's safe-haven channel rather than through trade.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Guidance divergence between these two central banks is as wide as the rate differential and points the same way. The RBA's 29 September statement was unanimous, judged that a further tightening of financial conditions is warranted, and retained the option explicitly in the words 'including increasing the cash rate target further if needed'; Bullock reinforced it by calling the fuel price increase permanently higher and — the single most currency-relevant line in either dossier — naming the exchange rate the most important channel through which policy operates. A central bank that wants tighter conditions and identifies FX as the main transmission channel has no incentive to talk its currency down. The SNB moved the other way: in June it said its willingness to intervene should remain increased, and in September it dropped the qualifier and reverted to the standard formulation, which is a central bank signalling comfort with a weaker franc while the franc depreciates roughly 3% trade-weighted. The credibility differential compounds the divergence. The market prices the RBA's stated hiking option at roughly a fifth of its probability and prices the SNB at nearly 50% for a hike its own three-year conditional forecast says is unnecessary and that 60% of a Swiss Bankers Association survey says will not happen before 2028. Both mispricings resolve in the pair's favour. The sequence matters too: the RBA decides on 2026-11-03 and again on 2026-12-08 before the SNB decides at all on 2026-12-10, so Australia sets the tone of the cross for the entire tactical window.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the guidance divergence persists but its resolution concentrates into a single date, 2026-12-10, which is the only scheduled Swiss policy communication inside the horizon and therefore the most consequential event for this cross on either timeframe. The structural asymmetry favours the pair: the SNB meets four times a year, provides minimal forward guidance by design, and has published a conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% constructed on an unchanged 0.00% rate through 2028 — a three-year statement that no tightening is required. If it confirms that in December, roughly 75bp of embedded tightening leaves the Swiss front end and the franc weakens on the repricing alone, with no change in the policy rate. The RBA's guidance is more predictable than its peers' precisely because it has anchored its reaction function to a shock it has declared permanent, which under any standard framework means less scope to look through an inflation overshoot. The offsetting risk is symmetric in form but asymmetric in timing: a central bank that has told the market it will keep hiking has more to lose from stopping, and with Australian unemployment at a post-COVID high the probability that the RBA has to reverse its own guidance inside six months is not small — the 2026-11-03 and 2026-12-08 decisions are where its own forecast revisions would reveal whether it is marking inflation up or growth down. Confidence of 60 rather than higher reflects that the December Swiss binary is a coin flip on the market's own numbers and that it carries more of this verdict's error term than any other single event.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Event risk is asymmetric against this pair because both of the live near-dated binaries resolve toward the franc if they resolve badly, and neither has a clean Australian offset. The Iran war is on day 215 with Iran's seven-day Hormuz roadmap rejected and indirect UN General Assembly talks reduced to a sequencing dispute; a failure re-closes an export recovery that has reached 16.328mb/d, just under 80% of the pre-war baseline, and produces a simultaneous oil, equity and credit shock in which the base currency has the highest G10 risk beta and the quote currency is the first refuge. The second is French: OAT-Bund at 111.2bp is at a one-year high against a 74.2bp average, French debt is 119% of GDP, a EUR 54bn budget vote is pending in the second week of October, and the franc rather than the euro is the regional refuge — a channel with no Australian counterpart at all, so it is a one-sided pair risk. Against those, a benign resolution of either is only ambiguously pair-positive: a Hormuz settlement lifts global growth and Chinese demand, which helps the base currency, but removes the energy premium that is the stated foundation of the RBA's September hike, which hurts it. Australian domestic political risk is negligible with no federal election due until May 2028, and Swiss domestic political risk is effectively nil. The asymmetry — two identifiable downside triggers, no clean upside trigger — is what makes this Bearish rather than Neutral despite the modal path being uneventful.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the event set widens and the signs stop agreeing, which flattens the stance to Neutral. The Iran binary becomes genuinely two-sided and, importantly, its benign resolution is ambiguous rather than positive for this cross: a settlement collapses the energy premium, which removes the franc's haven bid and the Swiss headline-inflation impulse behind the market's December hike pricing — both pair-positive — while simultaneously removing the RBA's permanently-higher justification and the Australian rate advantage that is the pair's entire carry case — pair-negative and larger. The French channel remains one-sidedly negative but its mechanism has been tested repeatedly since 2024 and the market's response function has attenuated; 111.2bp is a one-year high rather than a crisis level. The one strategic event with a clean pair-positive sign is Chinese: the Central Economic Work Conference in December and the National People's Congress in March 2027 set the growth target and the stimulus envelope, and with Q2 GDP at 4.3% the case for a property or infrastructure package is strong — it would transmit through iron ore to the base currency with no offsetting Swiss channel. Tail probabilities over six months are roughly 25% for a Hormuz settlement, 15% for a renewed closure, 20% for a material Chinese stimulus and around 20% for a French government collapse; the signs do not net cleanly in either direction, which is the honest content of a Neutral.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: There is no fiscal differential worth trading between these two sovereigns and the honest reading is Neutral at relatively high confidence, because the evidence that the factor is immaterial is itself strong. Only three factors are non-zero: Policy and Rates at +0.1782 and Guidance at +0.0720 against External Balance at -0.1116. Six factors score exactly zero, covering 43% of the strategic weight, and that is not a rounding artefact — it is six genuine standoffs, where each dossier is bearish on its own currency for different reasons and the effects cancel. A score assembled from three factors out of ten is less reliable than one assembled from broad agreement, and the honest reading is that this is a carry call with one large, well-identified structural objection rather than a thesis with depth. Conviction is 2 rather than 3 for exactly that reason: the direction is real, the breadth is not, and a 12.9-point current-account gap running against a 16-point real-exchange-rate gap is the kind of offset that does not resolve quickly but does resolve.
strategic.rationale: At strategic weights the shape of the book changes while its direction does not. External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.18 and Guidance from 0.07 to 0.12 while Inflation and Growth falls from 0.16 to 0.10 and Flows from 0.12 to 0.06, so structural factors displace data-flow factors and the score falls from +0.3541 to +0.1386 without changing sign. Policy and Rates remains the dominant contribution at +0.1782, because a 460bp differential does not stop paying over six months — approximately 133 pips of accrual against a 0.57643 spot — and because the SNB sits on a 0.00% floor with no conventional easing room, which caps how far the gap can compress from the Swiss side. Guidance adds +0.0720 on a divergence that is both wide and dated: the market prices roughly 75bp of SNB tightening by September 2027 against a central bank whose own conditional forecast runs 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% on an unchanged rate through 2028, and the single scheduled Swiss event inside the horizon, 2026-12-10, is where that resolves. Against those, External Balance at -0.1116 is the serious objection and it is concrete rather than rhetorical: Australia runs a 3.67%-of-GDP current account deficit with the goods and services balance itself in deficit at AUD 5.1bn and net foreign debt at AUD 1,486bn, while Switzerland runs a 9.20%-of-GDP surplus with a net international investment position of CHF 986bn and a Q2 trade surplus that nearly doubled. Valuation says the same thing from the other side: the base currency's real effective exchange rate is 116.11, the highest in the block and up 9.97% in a year achieved while iron ore fell 7.14%, against a quote currency at 99.87 and down 2.83%. A currency cannot stay 16 real points rich against a widening surplus partner for six months without something giving. The two dossiers' standalone views interact unusually here: the base dossier is strategically Neutral on AUD and the quote dossier strategically Bearish on CHF, so the pair inherits a mild upward tilt from the quote leg alone, and the bilateral work mostly consists of checking whether Australia's external deterioration is large enough to overturn it — it is not quite, which is what +0.1386 says. What is priced is a forward curve that discounts the pair at roughly 4.89% annualised as the mechanical carry offset and assigns zero value to either the external gap or the real-valuation gap. Our expectation is that the carry is collected but that the external and valuation channels cap rather than extend the advance, so the path of least resistance is a decelerating grind rather than a trend. The dated catalysts are RBA 2026-11-03 and 2026-12-08, SNB 2026-12-10, the FOMC with projections on 2026-12-09 and the Chinese Central Economic Work Conference in December. Conviction is 2 because six of ten factors are genuine zeros, because the score rests on three lines, and because the one large negative is the factor least likely to be wrong — a measured surplus against a measured deficit.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically AUD/CHF remains the highest-carry long available in the G10 cross matrix at 460bp, but its ranking deteriorates relative to its tactical standing because the base leg's external position is the second-worst in the block at -3.67% of GDP while the quote leg's is the second-best at +9.20%. Among AUD longs it still outranks AUD/USD, where the differential is only 72.5bp and the carry-to-vol ratio collapses to 0.117, and AUD/NZD, where the differential is 185bp against a hiking RBNZ. Among CHF shorts it ranks behind EUR/CHF on efficiency — 250bp against 3.89% realised volatility, with the SNB's own focus pair isolating the policy thesis without a commodity or high-beta leg — and ahead of CHF/SEK and CHF/JPY on carry. The summary position is first on gross carry, mid-pack on risk-adjusted return, and last among franc shorts on tail behaviour.

strategic.path_expectation: The path should look like an L tilted upward: an early carry grind, a December test, then a plateau. Phase 1, October–November: a continuation of the tactical grind into 0.5812–0.5853, driven by the two RBA decisions and the absence of Swiss policy news. Phase 2, 8–17 December: the concentrated risk window — RBA on the 8th, FOMC with projections on the 9th, SNB on the 10th, ECB on the 17th, plus the year-end funding turn. All of the adverse outcomes would hit the pair in the same direction, so volatility should rise into it. Phase 3, January–March 2027: the advance slows as the external gap and Australia's 116.11 real exchange rate weigh on it, and the pair plateaus in the 0.58–0.59 area with carry rather than price providing the return. Pullback levels are 0.5706–0.5743 first and the 200-week average second. The 200-week falls about 3.4 pips a week, to roughly 0.5660 by the December cluster and 0.5605 by end-March. In December it therefore moves into the six-touch 0.56309–0.5672 band, so if the pair sells off into the SNB meeting it meets a support that is densest at exactly that point. consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast: No pair-level bank point-forecast for AUD/CHF was located. Nearest bank research: (1) Bank of America in June recommended a 3-month AUD/CHF digital call with a 0.5800 target (pair then 0.5619); the target was reached in late August and overshot to 0.58827 in September. (2) RBC Capital Markets Currency Report Card forecasts mild AUD appreciation on the best G10 carry and judges the carry case for shorting CHF holds over the next 6-12 months, calling the franc the most efficient short leg in G10 carry. (3) UBS (May) expects the franc to weaken further against higher-yielding, pro-risk currencies; Rabobank raised its 9-12 month EUR/CHF forecast to 0.95 from 0.94. This is directional bank commentary rather than a pair-level forecast number.
consensus_divergence.bank_consensus_forecast_source: Bank of America (via Investing.com), RBC Capital Markets Currency Report Card, UBS, Rabobank. Retail extrapolation sites that publish AUD/CHF 'forecasts' (Traders Union, CoinCodex, LongForecast and similar) were found and deliberately rejected as a category error.
consensus_divergence.our_tactical_view: Bullish, conviction 3, net weighted score +0.3541, overall confidence 64. The pair rises over two to four weeks on an underpriced RBA hike probability for 2026-11-03, a Swiss guidance vacuum that runs to 2026-12-10, and a benign risk tape that denies the franc its only mechanism for overriding a 460bp carry. Pair-level base case 0.5830.
consensus_divergence.our_strategic_view: Bullish, conviction 2, net weighted score +0.1386, overall confidence 58. The carry is collected but the advance decelerates, because a 12.9-point current-account gap and a 16-point real-effective-exchange-rate gap run against the pair and because the 2026-12-10 SNB assessment is a coin flip on the market's own numbers. Pair-level base case 0.5850 by end-March 2027.
consensus_divergence.divergence_direction: In line with the direction of the bank research located (RBC constructive AUD and bearish CHF; BofA bullish AUD/CHF; UBS and Rabobank bearish CHF), but more conservative than currency-by-currency commentary on the strategic horizon, where we weight the Australian external deterioration more heavily. Pass 2 notes we are further along than the banks: our tactical base is above BofA's achieved target.
consensus_divergence.divergence_magnitude: Not quantifiable against a pair-level consensus number. Pass-2 reference points: our tactical base of 0.5830 is 30 pips above BofA's achieved 0.5800 target; our six-month base of 0.5850 is about 250 pips above the stale aggregated 0.56 late-2026 figure; our expected values sit 67–196 pips above the forwards. Against market pricing, we put the 2026-11-03 RBA hike probability materially above the roughly 20% discounted, and the 2026-12-10 SNB hike probability materially below the roughly 50% discounted.
consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: We differ from the market rather than from the banks, and we do so on one bilateral factor the standalone currency views systematically understate: the simultaneity of the two mispricings. Taken separately, an underpriced RBA hike and an overpriced SNB hike are each ordinary observations. Taken as a cross, they compound — the same four-week window contains two Australian decisions and no Swiss one, so the hawkish leg has two scheduled opportunities to be proved right while the dovish leg has none to be proved wrong, and the Swiss hike pricing can only decay through data in the interim. Where we are more conservative than a naive combination of the two dossiers is strategic: we weight External Balance at 0.18 rather than 0.16 because the 12.9-point current-account gap and the 16-point real-exchange-rate gap between these two specific economies are the widest non-petroleum pairing in the block, and that offset is what takes the strategic score from a comfortable Bullish to a marginal one. Pass-2 addendum: BofA's 0.5800 target is the closest thing to a pair-level bank consensus; it agrees with the direction and has already been delivered, so the pair sits just below a target the market met. The one aggregated pair forecast found (aggregated bank research, market expectations and a sentiment survey) puts AUD/CHF at 0.54000 early 2026 then 0.56000 late 2026; it is stale relative to spot and its 0.5600 late-2026 level is 164 pips below spot, close to our strategic downside. Where pass 2 disagrees with pass 1 without re-scoring: the verdict's tactical edge rests heavily on the view that Swiss hike pricing is too rich and can only fade. September Swiss CPI at 1.0%, printed the day the pair had its widest range of the window, is the first evidence against that. If the early-November Swiss October CPI also prints at or above 1.0%, the dovish-SNB half of the 'two simultaneous mispricings' argument falls away, and the trade depends on the Australian leg and carry alone. That would still justify a Bullish direction on Factor 1's rate level, but not the tactical confidence assigned to Factor 6.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: The carry is the payoff and it is measured rather than forecast: approximately 21.8 pips a month and approximately 133 pips over six months at 460bp on a 0.57643 spot, with the futures roll paying wider still at -488.6bp annualised. On top of that, a resolution of either mispricing — a trimmed mean at or above 3.7% on 28 October taking November RBA pricing through 50%, or an uneventful SNB hold on 2026-12-10 removing roughly 75bp from the Swiss front end — repays through spot as well as accrual. Pass-2 levels: about +87 pips tactically and about +219 pips strategically including carry.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: Two identifiable ways to be wrong, and they are not symmetric. The smaller is a soft Australian trimmed mean at or below 3.4% on 28 October, which removes the tactical thesis in a single print without doing lasting damage to the carry. The larger is the SNB validating market pricing on 2026-12-10, which would convert the franc from a funding currency into one with a tightening cycle ahead of it and invalidate the largest single input to both horizons. Compounding both is the pair's shape: it is the G10's most convex risk-off expression, so a Hormuz failure or a French government collapse produces a move that is fast, large and uncompensated by 21.8 pips a month. Pass-2 levels: about -99 pips to the tactical stop, or about -194 pips to the strategic stop, with gap risk beyond either.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The horizons agree on direction and disagree on strength, and the disagreement is mechanical rather than interpretive. The same 460bp differential drives both, but the weight on External Balance rises from 0.06 to 0.18 and turns a 12.9-point current-account gap and a 16-point real-exchange-rate gap from an irrelevance into the largest single negative in the book, while the weight on Inflation and Growth falls from 0.16 to 0.10 and the factor flips from Bullish to Neutral as Australia's cost-push inflation becomes a margin contraction. Six factors are genuine zeros strategically against three tactically, so the strategic score rests on three lines while the tactical score rests on seven — same sign, much less breadth, which is precisely why conviction falls from 3 to 2 while the stance does not change.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Hold the same direction on both horizons but treat them as different trades. The tactical expression is a short-duration, catalyst-dependent long resolved by the Australian CPI on 28 October and the RBA decision on 2026-11-03, where the carry is incidental to the repricing. The strategic expression is a carry hold whose return is the 133 pips of six-month accrual rather than any expected spot appreciation, and whose principal risk is concentrated in a single fortnight — the FOMC on 2026-12-09, the SNB on 2026-12-10 and the year-end funding turn all land together, and all three would hurt the pair in the same direction if they go wrong. Position sizing should reflect that the pair's carry accrues linearly while its adverse tail arrives instantaneously. Pass-2 practical mapping: take profit on the tactical position in 0.5812–0.5853 after 3 November; re-establish the strategic carry position only on dips into 0.5706–0.5743, or near the falling 200-week average; decide by 7 December, ahead of the 8–10 December cluster, whether to cut strategic exposure to quarter-size, with the deciding signals being the Swiss October and November CPI prints and December SNB hike pricing.

catalysts.rationale: This is the first positioning read after the valuation date and after the 1 October sell-off. A narrowing of the CHF leveraged short beyond −8% of open interest would show the covering in this pair's book has begun; a further build deepens the squeeze risk that is Factor 4's tactical negative.

catalysts.event: French National Assembly vote on the EUR 54bn budget (second week of October; exact date approximate, source gives 2026-10-W2)
catalysts.rationale: In a government collapse, the franc rather than the euro is the regional refuge, and Australia has no offsetting channel. A break in OAT-Bund through 125bp would hit the crowded franc short directly.

Australian unemployment reached a post-COVID high of 4.6% in August with the entire 39,000 employment gain part-time and full-time down 6,000. A third consecutive rise would start pricing an RBA pivot and undercut the base leg's entire rate advantage; a fall back to 4.5% with full-time gains removes the main domestic obstacle to a November hike. There is no Swiss counterpart release in the window, so the surprise transmits one-sidedly to the pair.

catalysts.event: ABS Consumer Price Index, Australia, September quarter 2026
catalysts.rationale: The highest-impact release for this cross in the tactical window and the trigger for the whole tactical thesis. It lands six days before the 2026-11-03 RBA decision, which the market discounts at roughly 20%, and the August monthly indicator has already re-accelerated to 4.0% with trimmed mean stuck at 3.6% for three months. A trimmed mean at or above 3.7% reprices November through 50% and widens a differential the quote leg has no scheduled means of answering before 2026-12-10.

A non-USD cross captures the Fed only through the vehicle-currency and risk channels, and those partly cancel: a hawkish outcome keeps the carry regime intact, which favours the pair's zero-rate quote leg losing more, but also keeps the dollar at the US-exceptionalism end of the smile where the high-beta base leg underperforms. The net effect is small and its sign depends on whether dollar strength arrives with or without funding stress.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision; ABS International Trade Price Indexes (September quarter)
catalysts.rationale: The ECB matters to this cross through the quote leg: the SNB-ECB spread drives EUR/CHF and therefore the franc's trade-weighted path, and a hawkish euro-area hold sustains the franc's broad weakness. The Australian trade price indexes give the first hard read on the September quarter terms of trade after a 1.6% June-quarter fall, with coal up 36.72% and copper up 35.84% against iron ore down 7.14% — genuinely uncertain composition.

catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia, Monetary Policy Board decision
catalysts.rationale: The first of two scheduled base-leg decisions and the resolution point for the tactical thesis. The Board hiked unanimously on 29 September and retained the explicit option of raising further, yet roughly 20% is discounted. Because the quote leg's central bank does not meet until 2026-12-10, a hike or a hawkish hold widens a 460bp differential with no scheduled Swiss answer available for five weeks, which is the cleanest bilateral asymmetry in the calendar.

catalysts.event: Swiss October CPI (FSO) (early November; exact date approximate, source gives 2026-11-W1)
catalysts.rationale: Added in pass 2, and now the most important Swiss datum before the SNB meeting. September printed 1.0%, above the threshold the CHF dossier treated as validating the SNB's own dovish forecast. A second print at or above 1.0% would make the market's ~50% December hike pricing look correct and remove the Swiss half of Factor 6's tactical edge. A print back at or below 0.8% restores it.

On the trajectory from 4.5% in July to 4.6% in August this release determines whether 5.0% Australian unemployment arrives inside the strategic window. A print at 4.8% or above begins the pivot repricing that would remove the base leg's rate support and turn the strategic Bullish into something weaker; a fall to 4.4% extends the RBA's room to tighten into 2027 and with it the pair's carry ceiling.

The monthly indicator has been the leading signal for the quarterly series, moving from 3.5% in July to 4.0% in August while trimmed mean held at 3.6%. An October reading showing headline rolling over as the Brent retracement feeds through would confirm the energy impulse fading, which erodes the base leg's hiking rationale faster than it erodes the quote leg's — Swiss core at 0.40% was never energy-driven.

catalysts.event: Reserve Bank of Australia, Monetary Policy Board decision
catalysts.rationale: The last Australian decision of 2026 and the one at which the cumulative tightening question is settled two days before the SNB speaks. If November delivered, this is the hold that defines the peak of the pair's carry; if November held, this becomes the live meeting with October and November data in hand. Either way it sets the base leg's terminal rate immediately before the quote leg's only scheduled communication of the horizon.

catalysts.event: FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: The December projections determine whether the dollar stays parked at the exceptionalism end of the smile through the strategic window, which is the regime in which carry trades are paid and the pair's zero-rate quote leg is the preferred short. It also lands in the same fortnight as the year-end funding turn, when cross-currency basis historically widens and funding currencies squeeze higher — a pair-negative risk correlated with the SNB event the next day.

catalysts.event: Swiss National Bank, quarterly monetary policy assessment
catalysts.rationale: The single most consequential scheduled event for this cross on either horizon and the only quote-leg policy communication inside the strategic window. The market prices nearly a 50% chance of a 25bp hike against an SNB conditional forecast of 0.7%/0.8%/0.8% built on an unchanged 0.00% rate. A hold with no tightening signal removes roughly 75bp of embedded Swiss tightening and widens the pair's differential in forward space without either bank moving; a hike or a normalisation reference inverts the largest single input to this verdict.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council with updated staff projections
catalysts.rationale: The meeting at which the euro-area cycle resolves, and it reaches AUD/CHF through the franc's trade-weighted path rather than directly. A December ECB hike widens the SNB-ECB gap to 275bp and keeps the franc broadly offered, which is pair-positive; an explicit signal that the cycle is complete caps the franc's depreciation against its largest trading partner and, by extension, against the Australian dollar.

catalysts.event: China Central Economic Work Conference (December, second week; exact date approximate, source gives 2026-12-W2)
catalysts.rationale: The one clean pair-positive event in the strategic window. A property or infrastructure package would lift iron ore from USD 96.59 straight into the base currency, and the franc has no commodity channel to offset it. It is the main route to the strategic upside case of 0.6000.

assumptions: Price series, verbatim from the payload: dataPoints 130; dateRange 2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02; spot 0.57643; spotDate 2026-10-02; computationRange 2007-12-24 to 2026-10-02 (4900 weekday bars); dataQuality: 'AUD/CHF: 4900 weekday bars in the store (2007-12-24 to 2026-10-02); 1007 weekly, 500 monthly; 130 daily bars passed downstream (2026-04-06 to 2026-10-02), which is the 1-6 month strategic horizon'.

Spot-date gap: the spotDate (2026-10-02) is one session after the valuation date (2026-10-01). Every level, pip distance, percentage, breakeven and forward outright is anchored to 0.57643; no fresher web quote was substituted. The 2026-10-01 close was 0.57604, so the gap is 3.9 pips.

Verdict carried verbatim: all factor stances, confidences, evidence types, weights, weight-adjustment reasons, weighted scores, net stances, convictions, overall confidences, rationales, rankings and the pass-1 consensus and cross-horizon blocks are reproduced from the pass-1 Direction Verdict without re-scoring. Two things are added and labelled pass-2: disagreements stated in the report's own words (mainly the effect of the post-cut Swiss September CPI print of 1.0% on Factor 6's tactical edge, sourced from the CHF dossier's assumptions block as post-valuation context) and execution levels in a Factor 9 addendum.

Realised volatility discrepancy: the verdict's Factors 1 and 9 cite 60-day realised volatility of 5.65%, taken from the dossiers. The payload's realisedVol.60d is 5.92%. The verdict text is unchanged, but every pass-2 metric uses the payload figure. On it, the carry-to-vol ratio is 0.78 against realised and 0.73 against the estimated implied volatility.

Moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes over the whole stored history. The duration above the 200-week average (about seven weekly closes) is back-calculated by assuming the reported slope of −0.000342 a week held constant; it is approximate.

Implied volatility: the pair-level implied volatility (6.345% / 6.282% / 6.562%) is a triangle estimate from the ADU and CHU legs, not a quote, and is documented as running low. No risk reversal, IV percentile or cross-currency basis is available for this pair.
Forward points are derived by linear extrapolation from the −488.6bp futures roll (6AZ6 to 6AH7). They are not quoted and are not a policy differential.

Scenario probabilities and expected values: probabilities are pass-2 judgements set at 50/25/25. Expected values are probability-weighted pip outcomes from 0.57643, shown before and after carry. For the strategic downside, half the carry is assumed, because a downside realised early in the horizon accrues less.

Bilateral trade: IMF DOTS 2024 figures were used as supplied. The mirror statistics are inconsistent: Australia records a USD 1.6bn deficit with Switzerland, while Switzerland's reported flows imply the opposite. This is flagged in Factor 5.
Weight adjustments are pass 1's and sum to 1.00 on both horizons.

Research scope and rejected sources: chart-pattern searches found no current attributable named pattern; TradingView and CentralCharts ideas are dated (several reference levels near 0.53–0.56) and were not used for levels. Retail model-forecast sites (Traders Union, CoinCodex, LongForecast and similar) were reviewed and rejected as pair consensus. Support and resistance come only from the payload's computed zones.

Citation labelling: pass 1's single citation is RBC Capital Markets' Currency Report Card, labelled [P1-1] in the factor blocks to keep it distinct from the numbered pass-2 research list. It was not re-accessed in pass 2.

Formatter note: catalysts dated only by week in the source (2026-10-W2, 2026-11-W1, 2026-12-W2) are given approximate calendar dates (2026-10-12, 2026-11-02, 2026-12-07) to satisfy the date format; the AUD CFTC percentile and pair IV percentile are not stated in the source (null for base_cftc_percentile and iv_percentile); quote_cftc_percentile 0 reflects 'the most stretched reading in the cached sample'; dossier dates are not stated in the source and are set to the valuation date.
